advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread a `started_at` timestamp through `_call_with_keepalive` so tool-call keepalives report real elapsed time like the workflow-step path.
evidence: keepalive.py:35: `elapsed_s = 0.0 if started_at is None else max(0.0, now - started_at)`
Contrast interpreter.py:514 which passes `started_at=_t_step` on completion
ABSENCE: no `started_at` is threaded through `_call_with_keepalive`, so both start and complete emits report elapsed=0.0 for tool calls
advisory.finding: The `tool-call-complete` keepalive is emitted without `started_at`, so on the occasions it does emit (>=25s after the last emission) it reports `elapsed=0.0s` regardless of how long the tool call actually ran. The sibling `workflow-step-complete` correctly passes `_t_step`, making the elapsed field inconsistent and misleading for tool-call telemetry.
scenarios: A single tool call runs >25s and the completion keepalive fires: it logs `elapsed=0.0s` even though the call took much longer, misdirecting anyone diagnosing which tool stalled.
advisory.suggested_fix: Capture `t0 = time.monotonic()` at the top of `_call_with_keepalive`, pass `started_at=t0` on both the start and complete `emit_keepalive` calls.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether global cross-operation keepalive coalescing is intended, or scope the coalescing window per run/operation so concurrent fan-out branches each surface progress.
evidence: keepalive.py:29: `if _last_emit_at is not None and now - _last_emit_at < KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S: return False`
runner.py:587-588 comment: "a slow/serial fan-out (e.g. the container per-child loop) is visible"
The single global window means N concurrent branches collectively emit at most one keepalive per 25s, not one per branch
advisory.finding: Keepalive coalescing state (`_last_emit_at`, `_call_index`) is process-global module state shared across all concurrent LLM/tool/workflow operations. Under the documented fan-out (container per-child loop), concurrent operations share a single 25s suppression window, so progress from one parallel branch suppresses keepalives for the others, weakening the multi-call progress visibility the feature exists to provide.
scenarios: Multiple gate LLM calls fan out concurrently in one process; only one keepalive prints per 25s across all of them, so a supervisor cannot tell whether all branches are progressing or one is hung.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a completion-phase keepalive (tool-call-complete / workflow-step-complete) emits, including when the dispatched step raises.
evidence: interpreter.py:513-514 `finally: emit_keepalive("workflow-step-complete", operation=sid, started_at=_t_step)` — no test drives a failing _dispatch to confirm the finally-path keepalive
agent_call.py:56-58 `_call_with_keepalive` emits `tool-call-complete` in a finally, but test_tool_keepalives_are_coalesced only ever observes `phase=tool-call-start`
ABSENCE: no keepalive message with phase=tool-call-complete or workflow-step-complete is asserted anywhere in the suite
advisory.finding: Completion-phase keepalives (tool-call-complete, workflow-step-complete) emitted from the new finally blocks are never asserted; the burst test coalesces them into the single start message, so no test verifies a completion keepalive ever emits or that the workflow-step-complete finally fires when _dispatch raises.
scenarios: A workflow step whose dispatch raises still needs its completion keepalive for progress visibility

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a keepalive test that advances monkeypatched monotonic past KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S between two emit_keepalive calls and asserts a second WARNING message emits.
evidence: keepalive.py:29 `if _last_emit_at is not None and now - _last_emit_at < KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S: return False` — the else branch (emit again once >=25s elapsed) has no test
test_tool_keepalives_are_coalesced asserts `len(messages) == 1` after a burst — only the suppression side
test_concurrent_keepalives_share_one_interval monkeypatches monotonic to a constant 100.0, so it can never cross the interval
Named violating input: two emit_keepalive calls with time.monotonic returning 100.0 then 130.0 should yield 2 messages; no test asserts this
blocking.finding: No test exercises keepalive RE-EMISSION after the coalescing interval elapses. Every keepalive test asserts exactly one message and only exercises suppression-within-interval; the re-emit-after-25s branch (the point of a keepalive during a long run) is untested, so a regression that fails to advance _last_emit_at, inverts the `now - _last_emit_at < KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S` comparison, or drops re-emission entirely would leave all tests green.
scenarios: A long gate run where the keepalive must fire repeatedly to satisfy the supervisor no-output budget the docs describe
blocking.suggested_fix: In test_llm_keepalive.py, monkeypatch keepalive.time.monotonic to return 100.0 then 130.0 across two emit_keepalive calls and assert two keepalive messages (call=1 then call=2).
